gaps.sentence: She has been a loyal ___ (EMPLOY) of the firm for twenty years.
gaps.hint: person needed: someone who works for the firm
gaps.explanation: An employee works for a company; 'employment' is the uncountable state of having a job.

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes a bit ___ ; add some salt (TASTE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: tasteless explains why salt is needed. An adjective follows 'tastes'.

gaps.sentence: We had a ___ view of the coast from the plane (SPECTACLE).
gaps.explanation: The adjective of 'spectacle' is spectacular; it modifies the noun 'view'.

gaps.sentence: Heavy snow made the mountain road ___ (PASS).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: impossible to travel through (im- + -able)
gaps.explanation: Heavy snow blocks the road, so the negative adjective 'impassable' (im- + pass + -able) is needed.

gaps.sentence: Try to be ___ when you cross the busy road (CARE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'be': careful (-ful). 'Carefully' is an adverb and cannot follow 'be'.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: The team played ___ and deserved to win (EXCELLENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'played': excellently (-ly).

gaps.sentence: He answered all the questions with great ___ (CONFIDENT).
gaps.explanation: 'Great' needs a noun: confidence. 'Confident' is the adjective.
